title: Marketplace onboarding — listing copy + certification checklist (WIP)
content:
Purpose / scope:
This doc is a working playbook for getting Redwood Inference listed in cloud marketplaces (initial focus: AWS Marketplace, then Azure and GCP). It combines proposed customer-facing copy, required artifacts, technical certification checklist, and a suggested timeline + owners.

Status note:
- Draft: lots of placeholder bullets and questions. Intended for review by Product, Solutions, Legal, and Engineering.
- Use-case: SaaS offering (hosted API) + dedicated offering (private/dedicated SKU where marketplace supports listing).

Top-level listing copy (short, long, bullets) — early drafts
1) Short title (<= 80 chars):
Redwood Inference — High-performance LLM inference platform (hosted & private)

2) Short description (1 sentence, ~150 chars):
Reduce inference latency and cost with Redwood Inference: managed hosted API, reserved GPU capacity, and private deployments — production-ready and observable.

3) Long description (2–3 paragraphs):
Redwood Inference is a developer-first inference platform that helps engineering teams ship LLM-powered features reliably and cost-effectively. Our hosted API supports generation, chat, embeddings, and reranking with streaming responses and function calling; Dedicated capacity offers reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput and data isolation; Private deployments provide VPC and on-prem options for regulated workloads.

Built for production: the platform includes intelligent batching and KV caching to lower per-token cost, a runtime optimized for modern attention kernels, and a console with per-route observability and rollout controls. Teams can pin model versions, run canary rollouts, and monitor quality regressions via evals tied to prompt sets.

4) Key bullets (for listing features section):
- Hosted REST API + SDKs for quick integration
- Dedicated GPU pools with SLA-backed capacity
- Private VPC/on-prem deployment options (HSM/KMS integrations)
- Cost controls: batching, caching, quantization recommendations
- Observability: token-level costs, latency breakdowns, per-model dashboards
- Rollouts & reliability: canary/A-B, automatic fallback policies

5) 1–2 CTAs (marketing copy):
- Try Redwood for free — get developer credits and a quickstart template for common LLM features.
- Contact sales for Dedicated or Private deployments and enterprise SLAs.

Marketplace-specific snippets (examples to adapt per vendor)
- AWS quick blurb: "Available on AWS Marketplace — subscribe to Redwood Inference for streamlined procurement and consolidated billing."
- Azure quick blurb: "Deploy Redwood with Azure Marketplace procurement; options for SaaS billing and private offers."

Technical & certification checklist (for marketplace listing teams) — work-in-progress
A. Business & procurement items
- [ ] Marketplace vendor account set up (GTM team)
- [ ] Master subscription agreement (legal) and marketplace terms reviewed
- [ ] Consolidated billing enabled (finance) — testing with sandbox invoices
- [ ] SKU mapping for products: Hosted (metered per-token), Dedicated (reservation SKU), Private (license/AM license)

B. Security & compliance artifacts
- [ ] SOC2 Type II summary + timing (or SOC2 in progress note)
- [ ] DPA / Data processing addendum template
- [ ] Privacy policy (public link) and documentation for data residency options
- [ ] Pen test summary (redacted) or vulnerability disclosure program link

C. Technical artifacts for listing submission
- [ ] Product icon (512x512 PNG) + architecture diagrams (SVG & PNG)
- [ ] 1–2 minute product explainer video (MP4) and transcript
- [ ] Example API integration guide (short code snippets) and SDK links (npm/pypi)
- [ ] Pricing matrix: per-token rates, embedding units, reserved capacity tiers — mapped to marketplace SKU pricing model
- [ ] Test account credentials / onboarding plan for marketplace validation team (rotate secrets, time-limited)

D. Integration & entitlement (engineering + platform)
- [ ] Support for marketplace entitlement API (license activation, customer mapping) — stub endpoint & integration test
- [ ] Metering pipeline: events that drive billing (per-token, per-embedding counts) — export format and sampling examples
- [ ] Billing reconciliation docs: how metering maps to invoices and Redwood internal accounting (finance + infra)
- [ ] Automated provisioning scripts (Terraform/ARM/GCP) for private trial envs (for vendor validation)

E. Ops & support readiness
- [ ] Marketplace support playbook (first-24h response, escalation paths)
- [ ] Onboarding checklist for customers who subscribe via marketplace (credentials, quotas, contact points)
- [ ] Observability snapshot pack for vendor validation (dashboards + sample traces)

F. UX/marketing QA items
- [ ] Short description trimmed to vendor character limits (AWS: 1 line, Azure: 300 char preview, etc.)
- [ ] Screenshots: Console onboarding flow, per-route dashboard, billing view (anonymized)
- [ ] SEO keywords and search terms for marketplace search (LLM inference, low-latency inference, dedicated GPU, managed inference)

Open questions / decisions (needs cross-functional input)
- Do we list Dedicated as a separate SKU or as an add-on to Hosted? (Pros/cons: procurement simplicity vs. clarity on isolation)
- For meter types: use "per-token generated" or "per-token interaction"? Need alignment with finance for invoicing precision and with infra on metering granularity.
- How do we handle trials for Dedicated / Private (do we issue time-limited entitlements or coupon codes)?
- Azure and GCP have different procurement models (private offers, marketplace subscriptions). Draft playbook should include per-vendor steps — need SME from each cloud.

Suggested timeline (high level)
- Week 0–2: finalize short + long copy, product assets (icons, screenshots), and pricing mapping (GTM + Finance + Product).
- Week 3–4: engineering: entitlement API + metering endpoint; infra: test sandbox tenant for vendor validation.
- Week 5: submit AWS listing + respond to vendor validation. Mirror process for Azure/GCP in parallel where possible.

Quick notes / scratchpad (choppy, for follow-ups)
- Capture example invoice that shows per-token lines — TODO ask Finance for sample (JIRA: GTM-412)
- We might compress the long desc for Azure listing since their preview windows are narrow — Miguel to make a 280-char variant
- Marketplace validation often requests a test flow that creates an account and calls an API endpoint — ensure provisioning script can create ephemeral demo accounts

References & attachments to prepare for submission
- architecture-diagram-v2.svg (in /marketplace-assets)
- product-explainer-30s.mp4 (internal S3 link)
- SOC2-summary-2025.pdf (legal folder)
- sample-metering-export.csv (infra/tests)

Next immediate steps (this week)
- [ ] Miguel: finalize three variants of the short description (AWS/Azure/GCP) — due 2026-03-05
- [ ] Priya: spin up entitlement stub + docs for validation team — due 2026-03-08
- [ ] Tom: provide sample invoice format + mapping doc — due 2026-03-06
- [ ] Legal (Lena): flag any marketplace T&Cs that may require contract exceptions — note by 2026-03-07

Notes for reviewers:
- Treat wording as draftable; we want to land on language that is vendor-friendly (concise) but also accurate for legal/finance.
- Add any past lessons learned from prior marketplace submissions (search Confluence: "marketplace-postmortems").

Inline copy candidates (pick one per field)
- Short headline options (pick one):
  A) "Redwood Inference — Fast, reliable LLM inference for production"
  B) "High-throughput LLM inference: Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments"
  C) "Production-grade LLM serving with cost & observability controls"

- 1-sentence CTA options:
  1) "Start a free trial — deploy in minutes with SDKs and example prompts."
  2) "Contact sales to configure Dedicated or Private deployments with SLAs."

---
End of draft.

(Internal drafting notes: save iterative copies to /marketplace-assets/drafts with date suffix, tag PRs that change pricing table, include a validation checklist per vendor that maps to this master checklist.)
